model_name: Expected incident radiant heat from active-burning probabilities or integrated one-hour wildfire forecasts
probability_semantics: Radiation-only: P(cell actively burns at an instant). Integration input: P(first new burning during next exact hour), explicitly converted to time-mean/endpoint active occupancy.

sources.title: Verification and Validation of Commonly Used Empirical Correlations for Fire Scenarios
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.location: Section 6.1, Equation (6.1), printed page 39, PDF page 53
sources.supported_role: Isotropic point-source radiation equals radiative fraction times HRR times receiver cosine, divided by 4*pi*distance squared.
sources.package_extension: Integrate infinitesimal isotropic emitters uniformly over each cell footprint and prescribe their common elevation rather than infer flame height.

sources.title: The NIST 3 Megawatt Quantitative Heat Release Rate Facility
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.location: Introduction, Equation (1), printed page 1, PDF page 8
sources.supported_role: For a known combustion heat, HRR equals mass-loss rate times combustion heat; complex/charring materials can have variable combustion heat.
sources.package_extension: The optional fuel converter assumes consumed mass per unit area is released at constant rate over a supplied burning duration.

sources.title: Thermal Radiation from Large Pool Fires
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.location: Section 3, printed page 3; Equation (1); point-source discussion and Equation (7)
sources.supported_role: Provides atmospheric-transmission and source-geometry context and warns that a single-point source can misrepresent radiation within a few fire diameters.
sources.limitation: This large-pool-fire/combustible-gas report does not validate the footprint model for wildfires or establish near-flame accuracy.

sources.title: Measurements of convective and radiative heating in wildland fires
sources.location: US Forest Service author publication record and abstract
sources.supported_role: Wildland-fire measurements distinguish irradiance from convective heating/cooling and show that their relative contributions depend on fuel/environment.
sources.limitation: Supports radiation-only scope; it was not used as a calibration dataset.
sources.access_status: Primary author-agency publication record and abstract inspected online

sources.title: Fuel Characteristic Classification System Fuelbeds
sources.location: Product Description, reference fuelbed assignment and fuel loading / Consume Input Tables paragraphs
sources.supported_role: LANDFIRE maps vegetation to FCCS reference fuelbeds; reference attributes include loading in tons per acre, useful as physical fuel inputs.

sources.title: Fuel Characteristic Classification System version 3.0: technical documentation

sources.title: Global Burning Properties of Little Bluestem, Excelsior and Douglas Fir
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology

sources.title: Heat transfer and fire spread
sources.supported_role: Porous-bed approximation: residence minutes = 8 times particle diameter or thickness in inches.
sources.limitation: Fuel-bed porosity can strongly change residence; not universal complete flame extinction.

sources.title: The Rothermel surface fire spread model and associated developments: A comprehensive explanation
sources.location: Sections 3.2.3-3.2.5, printed pages 21-24; section 4.2, printed page 27
sources.supported_role: Characteristic SAV surface-area weighting and residence_minutes = 384 / SAV_ft_inverse; exact SI residence_seconds = 75590.55118110236 / SAV_m_inverse.
sources.limitation: Passing-front residence excludes indefinite trailing edge and assumes no fuel-bed packing effect.

sources.title: Experimental development of a fire management model for jarrah (Eucalyptus marginata Donn ex Sm.) forest
sources.supported_role: Individual oven-dry jarrah twig residence_seconds = 0.871 * diameter_mm**1.875, tested diameter 1-16 mm.
sources.limitation: Individual 10 cm twigs in still air; not a general fuelbed, species or moisture law.

sources.title: Flame residence times and rates of weight loss of eucalypt forest fuel particles
sources.supported_role: Peer-reviewed follow-up on fuel-particle size, eucalypt leaves and round wood; leaves comparable to 4 mm wood.
sources.limitation: Exact implemented power law verified in 1994 thesis; full 2001 paper equation not claimed as directly inspected.

sources.title: Flame temperature and residence time of fires in dry eucalypt forest
sources.supported_role: Mean main-front residence 37 seconds, standard deviation 14 seconds, n=77; separates later continuous/intermittent flames.
sources.limitation: Elevated thermocouple temperature threshold in dry eucalypt forest; not a universal complete flame-out time.

sources.title: QES-Fire: a dynamically coupled fast-response wildfire model
sources.supported_role: Model precedent for time-on-fire gating against residence time and coefficient approximately 75591 s/m divided by SAV_m_inverse.
sources.limitation: Implementation precedent does not validate this package or transfer its model performance.

additional_modeling_assumptions: A cell indicator activates a uniform footprint over its entire area using whole-cell averaged conditional HRR density; partial burning coverage must be reflected in that density.
Infinitesimal emitters are isotropic at one elevation above upward-facing horizontal receivers.
Conditional source strengths are prescribed; probabilities mean active burning, not cumulative burned area or new ignition.
Atmospheric transmission is one scalar shared by all paths; path-dependent absorption and geometric blocking are omitted.
Linearity of expectation does not require cell independence.
Only supplied cells emit; exterior source contributions are omitted.
Synthetic demo parameters are illustrative and are not fitted to wildfire measurements.

The integrated forecast converts first-new-burning probability for an exact one-hour endpoint through a Uniform(0,3600s) conditional ignition time and a supplied deterministic constant-emission duration.
Time-mean source occupancy and endpoint source occupancy are distinct; mean heat flux multiplied by 3600s gives expected incident radiant energy per area during the forecast interval.
Cumulative burned state is not active combustion. Existing fire contributes only when initial active probability and remaining combustion duration are explicitly supplied.
Unknown model probabilities remain unknown. Bounds permit those probabilities to range over [0,1] only while prescribed combustion, geometry and timing assumptions remain fixed.

Ecological loading is a reference estimate. Partial lookup coverage requires an explicit unmapped-loading fallback, blended by mapped coverage; consumed fraction, duration, effective heat and radiative fraction remain caller assumptions.
The integrated example uses retrospective arrival/final-extent-derived current burned state and is not operational live forecast validation.
Flame residence at a fixed fuel point is assigned to representative raster locations; subcell propagation and exact flame geometry are unresolved.
Known or point-estimate arrival scenario uses activity on the half-open interval [arrival,arrival+residence). Unknown arrival remains unknown.
The FBFM40 catalog describes reference surface-front fuels; nonburnable, custom and missing codes require explicit scenario overrides, recorded separately.
Residence duration in the heat bridge must equal combustion duration; consumed fuel fraction must refer to the modeled flaming phase.
The active-flame example retains zero nominal flames and unthresholded probability coordinates; no active-flame observational calibration is claimed.
validation_status: Analytic/numerical verification of this mathematical model is separate from experimental wildfire validation; no experimental validation is claimed.
flame_residence_semantics: Estimated surface-front flaming at representative grid locations under explicit reference-fuel and conditional-arrival assumptions; particle flame-out available as a separate laboratory scenario.
